# ona_projects (Data Source)

List Gitpod projects in the organization. Filters are combined, so a project must match all of the ones that are set; list filters match a project when any of their values does.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "ona_projects" "by_repository" {
  remote_uris = ["https://github.com/combor/terraform-provider-ona"]
}

data "ona_projects" "most_popular" {
  sort = {
    field = "popularity"
    order = "SORT_ORDER_DESC"
  }
  limit         = 10
  include_count = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `creator_ids` (List of String) Only return projects created by these subjects.
- `include_count` (Boolean) Whether to request a bounded total count of matching projects in `total_count`.
- `limit` (Number) Maximum number of projects to return. Pages stop being fetched once this many projects are collected. By default all matching projects are returned.
- `project_ids` (List of String) Only return projects with these IDs.
- `remote_uris` (List of String) Only return projects whose initializer git `remote_uri` exactly matches one of these URIs.
- `runner_ids` (List of String) Only return projects that use environment classes from these runners.
- `runner_kinds` (List of String) Only return projects that use environment classes from runners of these kinds, such as `RUNNER_KIND_REMOTE`.
- `search` (String) Case-insensitive search across project name, project ID, and repository name.
- `sort` (Attributes) Order of `projects`. Defaults to `id` ascending, which is creation order and stays stable between runs. `popularity` ranks projects by recent environment creation activity and is recomputed periodically, so its order can change between runs. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sort))

### Read-Only

- `projects` (Attributes List) Matching projects, in `sort` order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--projects))
- `total_count` (Number) Total number of matching projects, regardless of `limit`. Set only when `include_count` is true. The API bounds this count, so check `total_count_relation` to see whether it is exact.
- `total_count_relation` (String) `COUNT_RESPONSE_RELATION_EQ` when `total_count` is exact, or `COUNT_RESPONSE_RELATION_GTE` when there are at least `total_count` matching projects.

Required:

- `field` (String) Field to sort by: `id` or `popularity`.
- `order` (String) Sort order: `SORT_ORDER_ASC` or `SORT_ORDER_DESC`.

Read-Only:

- `technical_description` (String) Detailed technical description of the project.
